findings.message: Now that the stopping token is passed to SendPingAsync, a shutdown during a ping cycle is treated as an unexpected ping failure: each in-flight device logs a Warning and is reported offline, and the code then tries to write that false 'offline' state to the database. SendPingAsync(..., cancellationToken: cancellationToken) throws OperationCanceledException when the token is cancelled. The only handler that catches it is `catch (Exception ex) { _logger.LogWarning(ex, "Unexpected error pinging {IpAddress}", ipAddress); return false; }`, so the exception is not rethrown. CheckDeviceAsync then sees `device.IsOnline != isOnline`, sets IsOnline=false and OnlineSince=null, and calls UpdatePcDeviceAsync(device, cancellationToken). The save is probably stopped only because SaveChangesAsync throws on the already-cancelled token. Nothing filters this case, e.g. `catch (OperationCanceledException) when (cancellationToken.IsCancellationRequested) { throw; }`.

The new troubleshooting hint (install iputils-ping, grant CAP_NET_RAW) is logged only at Debug, so on the shipped configuration a deployment where ping keeps failing just shows every device as offline and the hint never appears. `_logger.LogDebug(ex, "Ping failed for {IpAddress}. If running on Linux, ensure 'iputils-ping' is installed and the process has CAP_NET_RAW ...")`. Both docker-compose.yaml and dev/docker/docker-compose.yaml set `Serilog__MinimumLevel__Default=Information`. The PlatformNotSupportedException branch warns only once per process (`Interlocked.CompareExchange(ref _platformNotSupportedLogged, 1, 0)`) and then returns false silently on every later cycle.

The change adds an unpinned OS package to the final runtime image. iputils-ping installs a capability-bearing ping binary, which widens the image's attack surface, and nothing records the package's version or why it is needed beyond a comment. `apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends gosu iputils-ping` has no version pin. The app runs as appuser via `exec gosu appuser "$@"` in docker-entrypoint.sh, so .NET's Ping falls back to the external ping utility, and this package supplies it. It is a necessary new runtime dependency and should be recorded as one.

The change introduces a runtime requirement for device status monitoring (a ping utility, and possibly CAP_NET_RAW) but no install or troubleshooting doc mentions it, so manual-setup users on Linux and anyone running with a custom compose that drops capabilities get no guidance. The only reference to the requirement is inside the Debug log string at DeviceMonitoringService.cs:182. A search for iputils, NET_RAW, ICMP and cap_add across the README, docs/ and the compose files finds nothing.

No test covers the new behaviour: the one-time PlatformNotSupportedException warning or the cancellation now passed into the ping. The existing ping test cannot tell whether a ping succeeded. The diff changes no test files. In test/API/DeviceMonitoringServiceTests.cs, CheckAllDevicesAsync_PingsDevicesWithIpAddress pings loopback and asserts `UpdatePcDeviceAsync(..., Times.AtMostOnce)`, which passes whether ping succeeds, fails or is unsupported.

Cancellation during a ping is swallowed as an offline result, allowing a canceled monitoring check to complete successfully. The new SendPingAsync call receives cancellationToken, but its OperationCanceledException reaches catch (Exception) at line 184, which logs a warning and returns false. If the device was already offline, CheckDeviceAsync takes the unchanged-status branch without another cancellation-aware operation, so CheckAllDevicesAsync can return successfully instead of propagating cancellation.

The tests do not verify the new ping cancellation or one-time platform warning behavior. The diff changes only Dockerfile and DeviceMonitoringService.cs. The existing cancellation test throws from GetAllPcDevicesAsync before any ping occurs, while the loopback test permits zero updates with Times.AtMostOnce; neither exercises cancellation during SendPingAsync or the new PlatformNotSupportedException handler.
